title: Curated model provider catalog
description: The vendors this repository supports, as data. One row per provider id, in the order the rows were added. A base URL and an OAuth origin policy are written here and nowhere else: the Zig build turns this file into typed rows, so a value it does not hold does not compile, and `goap check` fails a non-test Go or Zig literal that spells a catalogued base URL. The names of the environment variables a credential arrives in, and the base URL overrides, are read through this file and are not yet gated. A provider id and a wire id stay literals in code; the id list is what a user-authored custom provider may not reuse. A row whose `base_url_source` is not `static` has no endpoint, because its default is credential-declared, derived, or a local default the code still owns. Every member is optional except `id`, because a curated row records what is known, and an absent member is unknown rather than empty. Credentials are never catalogued, only the names of the environment variables a provider is read from.

authKind.description: How a credential for this provider reaches it. An empty list means this repository records no credential path for the vendor, which is not the same as the vendor needing none.

offering.description: How a row's endpoint is paid for: a prepaid coding plan, a seat subscription, or metered tokens against an API key. A row is a vendor's *offering* rather than the vendor itself, because a coding plan or a subscription is a different endpoint reached under the same credential.

status.description: Where this row sits in the curated list. `current` rows are the ones the list names first; `supported` rows are available but not named first; `withheld` records a row the list does not offer, so an id a user cannot shadow stays recorded. A row with no status is `supported`.

baseUrlSource.description: Where a request's base URL comes from when no model names one. `static` means the endpoints below are the defaults; `credential` means the credential records the endpoint; `derived` means the implementation assembles it from configuration; `local_default` means a local development endpoint that an operator overrides for a hosted one.

region.description: The region this endpoint serves, for a provider that ships one endpoint per region. An endpoint with no region is the provider's only one.

oauthOrigin.description: The origins an OAuth credential may be sent to. A provider with no policy here is one whose credential is not origin-bound, and the implementation answers that itself.

domain.description: Any host under this domain, which covers an enterprise tenant of a per-tenant provider.

id.description: The provider id this repository reserves, which a user-authored custom provider may not reuse.

credential_env.description: Environment variables a credential is read from, in the order they are tried. The names, never the values.

base_url_env.description: Environment variables that override the base URL for this provider.

region_env.description: Environment variable naming the region, for a provider with one endpoint per region.

wires.description: The API or wire identifiers this provider is reached with.

endpoints.description: The static default endpoints. Absent for a provider whose base URL is credential-declared, derived, or a local default.

models_endpoint.description: Path appended literally to the base URL a request to this row would use — an endpoint's `base_url` including its own path, or the base a credential or a local default resolves to; never a URL join against the origin, and never relative to the host. The listing is that concatenation, so `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` with `/models` is `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/models`. One path serves the whole row, appended to every endpoint the row has, which is how `kimi` lists from two regional bases. It begins with `/` and names the vendor's own listing, so a base already ending in a version segment takes `/models` rather than `/v1/models`. Absent when the provider publishes no listing of its own.
